info.title: Universal Book Translator API
info.description: Industrial asynchronous bilingual translation microservice with SSE streaming.

post.description: Exchange the API key for a same-origin session cookie. The console's ``EventSource`` stream, page-preview ```` elements and download links cannot attach an ``X-API-Key`` header, so on a keyed server the UI would 401 on every one of them even though its fetches pass. The cookie carries a keyed *digest* of the service key (never the key itself), is HttpOnly + SameSite=Lax so it rides only same-origin browser requests, and is re-minted on every login. An open (keyless) server has nothing to exchange and returns ``authenticated: true`` without setting a cookie.

get.description:
Model/provider configuration actually in force (read-only).

The console used to render ``/model-profiles`` here, which is the
engine's capability *preset* table — fourteen hard-coded name patterns,
none of which is a configured model. This endpoint reports what the
engine will really call, which preset (if any) that model matches, and
the declared providers with credentials filtered out.

The forbidden-path list actually in force, for the console's panel.

The panel used to hardcode Unix paths, which on Windows described a
deny list this server does not have. This returns the same resolved
prefix tuple the request guard compares against, so what the panel
shows is what the server refuses — per platform, not per folklore.

The quality-estimation gate actually in force.

``qe_engine`` and ``qe_judge_enabled`` are two switches, and only the
second one scores anything — ``qe_engine = "tiered"`` on its own is a
no-op the pipeline merely warns about. Reporting them separately is what
lets the console say which one is off instead of a bare "QE not measured".

put.description:
Write the QE gate into ``ubt.toml [defaults]``.

The engine re-reads the file per job, so the change applies to the next
submitted job without a restart — which is the only useful behaviour here,
since a finished job is never rescored.

**The pair is written together by the console.** Selecting "tiered" sends
both ``qe_engine = "tiered"`` and ``qe_judge_enabled = true``; selecting
"heuristic" sends both back. Exposing the keys independently would let an
operator save the documented-but-useless ``tiered`` + judge-off state.

An explicit gate check even though the middleware already ran: this route
writes a file the engine then trusts, so it must not inherit a future
relaxation of the global filter (same rule as ``put_provider``).

get.description:
The page-egress gate in force right now.

Read from ``live_config()``, not the boot snapshot: a console toggle
must be visible the moment it lands, or the card lies exactly the way
the QE panel once did.

put.description:
Flip the page-egress gate for this server process.

The gate is fail-closed by design — the rendered pages of an
unpublished manuscript are the sensitive half of the payload — so a
console toggle must stay an explicit, confirmed act, and its reach must
be stated honestly. ``ubt.toml`` has no key for this field (the file
schema is ``[defaults]``/``[providers]`` only), so the write is a
runtime override on the config source: in force for every job this
process submits, gone at restart. Permanent opt-in stays where the
config module documents it: the ``UBT_ALLOW_PAGE_UPLOAD`` environment
variable.

get.description: One provider block, with the credential reduced to a mask.

put.description:
Create or update a ``[providers.<name>]`` block.

Writes ``ubt.toml``, which the engine re-reads per job, so the change
applies to the next submitted job without restarting the server.

**A credential is accepted only on a local, non-strict deployment.** See
:func:`ubt.api.provider_editor.credential_write_allowed` for the reasoning:
on loopback the caller could already read the file, so refusing the write
protected nothing while leaving a fresh install with no way to configure a
model. On a non-loopback bind or under strict auth the request is refused
and the message says where the secret belongs instead.

delete.description:
Remove one declared ``[providers.<name>]`` block.

Same posture as ``PUT``: the middleware gate runs twice on purpose, and
a block still named by ``[defaults]`` is refused with the referencing
field so the UI can tell the operator what to clear first.

Writes ``[defaults] provider``. Creating a block without this left a fresh

``can_translate`` stayed false because nothing named it.

get.description:
Engine Doctor self-check (the ``ubt doctor`` checklist as JSON).

Reuses the CLI's ``collect_checks`` so the console and the command line
report the same verdicts. ``probe=true`` additionally contacts the
provider endpoint (a live network call), so it is off by default.

Reads the **live** config, not the boot snapshot. ``app_config`` is built
once at startup, so a provider saved from the console an instant earlier
was invisible here: the form said "saved", the panel below it reported the
new provider as active, and this checklist still said ``API key FAIL`` and
``no draft model configured`` — two contradictory statements on one screen.

The console's security-boundary panel (real host + allowed roots).

Reports the host this request reached (loopback vs exposed), whether the
API-key gate is on, and the filesystem roots ``resolve_secure_path``
actually enforces — so the panel shows the live policy, not a hardcoded
sample.

get.description:
The job queue: every ledger in ``db_dir``, newest first.

Reads the durable store (one ``{job_id}.sqlite`` per job) so a restarted
console still lists finished jobs, and overlays live jobs with the
manager's in-memory progress (fresher than the ``job_meta`` row a run
only finalizes at the end).

``GET /jobs`` is also the console's Mission Control URL, so a browser
navigation (``Accept: text/html``) is answered with the SPA shell and
the client router resolves the screen; API clients get the JSON queue.

post.description:
Re-run a failed/cancelled job from its ledger checkpoints (PRD §4.2.4).

The pipeline resumes from the blocks still pending in the ledger, so no
finished segment is re-translated. The request is recovered from the
ledger when this process no longer has an in-memory record (the normal
case after a restart). New ledgers store the exact accepted request;
older ledgers are reconstructed from the run metadata they do carry.

Throw away a finished job's parse and rebuild it from the source file.

The one thing neither resume nor re-export can do. ``resume`` explicitly
refuses to re-fresh (it would discard the checkpoints it exists to keep),
and ``re-export`` only re-runs the export stage over the text already in
the ledger — so a fix to how the *source document* is parsed (block
splitting, table reconstruction, formula and figure crops) never reaches
a job that has finished. The delivered file keeps the old artefacts no
matter how many times it is re-rendered, because the ledger still names
the PNGs the old code cut.

This is expensive and destructive, and the API says so by requiring an
explicit call: every block is discarded and the whole book is
re-translated, incurring the provider cost of a first run. Human
revisions in the ledger are lost with it.

Only an in-session, terminal job can be re-parsed. Rebuilding the
request from the ledger alone would silently drop the model, preset and
output choices the run was made with — the same trap ``resume``
documents — so a job whose record is gone must be resubmitted.

delete.summary: Remove a finished job's ledger and deliverables from the console
delete.description:
Delete one job's history: the db_dir ledger plus its deliverable dir.

A running job must reach a terminal status first — deletion is history
management, not a stop button. A non-terminal queue-mode record is
likewise refused: the durable queue owns its rows (``prune_terminal``
is their lifecycle) and removing the ledger underneath a worker would
desynchronize its view.

get.description:
SSE: ``event: progress`` snapshots until one ``event: <status>`` terminal frame.

Both deployment modes emit that one contract (see ``progress_frame`` /
``terminal_frame``); the payload never depends on how the server was
started. Every frame carries an ``id:`` cursor, so a client reconnecting
with ``Last-Event-ID`` (header or ``?last_event_id=``) receives the
frames it missed before the live stream resumes (PRD §9.2).

List the deliverables a finished job actually left on disk.

A run may emit a complementary dual/mono render, an EPUB and the JSON
sidecars depending on its flags; the UI must render only what exists
rather than offer four fixed buttons. Keys match
:data:`DELIVERABLE_LABELS`.

Serve one deliverable by key (see :data:`DELIVERABLE_LABELS`).

``?inline=1`` renders the file in place (the console's preview pane)
instead of attaching it: no ``Content-Disposition: attachment``, and a
media type the browser can actually display. The response is served
under a CSP ``sandbox`` directive either way — the HTML deliverable is
generated from *book* content, which is untrusted input, so even a
fetched-directly preview runs scriptless in an opaque origin rather
than in the console's origin.

``?force=1`` takes a delivery the quality gate blocked. It exists for
the operator who has read the report and decided the partial book is
still worth shipping; without it a ``blocked`` verdict refuses the
reader-facing deliverables (see the check below).

A page of a job's finalized blocks for the workbench grid.

``status=issues`` returns everything the fault ribbon counts plus the
PE-queue members; a concrete ``BlockStatus`` value filters by lifecycle
status. Blocks are projected with their source/target, QE score, flags
and grouped issue kinds.
Fault-ribbon counts by issue kind, plus terminology drift detail.

post.description: Apply one human revision (ledger + shared TM), the L3 feedback path.

Re-render a finished job's deliverable from its current ledger text.

A human edit lands in the ledger, but the delivered file was rendered
before it — the reviewer saw the fix in the preview while the download
stayed stale. This re-runs the export stage over the current text and
overwrites the deliverable in place. No token is spent: every block is
already terminal, so only render + reports run.

get.description:
Terminology findings for one block, with the cascade size each implies.

Each finding carries the offending ``surface``, the ``expected``
rendering, and how many *other* blocks in the job carry the same
error — ``cascade_all`` for the whole book, ``cascade_subsequent`` for
blocks at or after this one. This is what the "fix all N" checkbox
counts.

post.description:
Replace one offending term surface across the job (PRD §5.2.2).

Rewrites the selected block and, per ``scope``, every matching block;
each rewritten block is promoted to a human revision and its pair fed
back to the shared TM, exactly like a manual edit.

get.description:
Re-compose one source page with the current ledger text, as PNG.

Reuses the delivery renderer for a single page,
so a human edit can be previewed without re-rendering the book. 503 when
the page has nothing to compose or the rasterizer is unavailable.

Rasterize the *source* PDF's page ``page`` as PNG.

The "before" half of the L3 pixel-witness view; pairs with
``/pages/{page}/preview`` (the composed "after"). 503 when the source is
missing or the rasterizer is unavailable.
List all currently registered model capability profiles.

post.description:
Bulk-import CSV/TSV/JSON pairs into the configured glossary file.

Mirrors the TM import: parsing is strict, so a malformed payload is a
422 rather than a silent partial import, and the file's existing format
is preserved row-for-row. Pairs with an empty side are skipped.

Stage a per-book glossary; returns the path a job submit accepts.

The console cannot send a filesystem path (browsers do not expose one),
and asking the operator to type a server-side path was a CLI reflex
wearing a web form. This stages the bytes the same way ``/jobs/upload``
stages source documents — timestamped, collision-free, inside the
managed uploads dir — and the returned ``path`` goes into the job's
``glossary`` field untouched.

Import TMX/JSON pairs into the shared TM (machine provenance by default).

An import is unverified, so the default ``machine`` provenance cannot
downgrade an existing ``human_pe`` row (the store's writeback enforces
that). Parsing is strict: a malformed payload is a 422, not a silent
empty import.

ModelProfile.title: ModelProfile
ModelProfile.description:
Declarative capability profile for one model on one provider.

Every field is a statement about the endpoint, so a profile is only ever
attached to a specific ``[providers.<name>]`` block or to the generic
fallback — never to a model *name* alone.

declared.title: Declared
declared.description: True when the operator declared it in [providers.*]

has_credential.title: Has Credential
has_credential.description: Whether this block's own credential resolves to a non-empty value. False for an unset ${VAR}: present in the file, unusable on the wire

authenticates.title: Authenticates
authenticates.description: Whether a call from this block can authenticate at all, counting UBT_LLM_API_KEY. Distinct from has_credential: a keyless block on a deployment that exports the generic variable does run

credential_issue.title: Credential Issue
credential_issue.description: Stable code for why the credential is unusable: 'unresolved_variable' when a ${VAR} reference has no value, 'missing' when nothing supplies one, null when it resolves

unresolved_vars.title: Unresolved Vars
unresolved_vars.description: Names of ${VAR} references in the block that resolve to nothing

credential_shadowed_by_env.title: Credential Shadowed By Env
credential_shadowed_by_env.description: True when this block holds a usable credential that UBT_LLM_API_KEY nevertheless outranks. A save is then inert until that variable is unset, and the form must say so rather than promise the next job

credential_hint.title: Credential Hint
credential_hint.description: A fixed mask when a credential is configured, never the value: the console needs to render 'already set', not to read the secret back

credential_in_file.title: Credential In File
credential_in_file.description: True when the block itself carries the credential

ProviderDetailResponse.title: ProviderDetailResponse
ProviderDetailResponse.description:
One provider block as the console may see it.

``has_credential`` / ``credential_in_file`` are booleans on purpose: whether a
key is configured decides whether the block can run at all, and a boolean is
the most that may be revealed about it.

**"Configured" means "resolves", not "is written".** A block may carry
``api_key = "${OPENCODE_API_KEY}"`` while that variable is unset; the loader
then hands the router an empty string and every call fails, so a form that
reported "credential set" for it promised an authentication the next job could
not perform. ``credential_issue`` names the two failure shapes by code, and
``unresolved_vars`` says which exports are missing — names only, never values.

make_default.title: Make Default
make_default.description: Also write [defaults] provider = name. The console sends this when creating a block, because a declared block that nothing points at is still a rehearsal — the state a fresh install was stuck in

api_key.title: Api Key
api_key.description: Credential for this provider block. Accepted only on a loopback, non-strict deployment; elsewhere the request is refused and the message says to use the environment or the file.

reasoning_dialect.title: Reasoning Dialect
reasoning_dialect.description: How the responses protocol spells a reasoning effort

supports_temperature.title: Supports Temperature
supports_temperature.description: Whether the endpoint accepts a temperature

supports_reasoning_effort.title: Supports Reasoning Effort
supports_reasoning_effort.description: Whether the endpoint accepts a reasoning effort

supports_system_prompt.title: Supports System Prompt
supports_system_prompt.description: Whether the endpoint accepts a system turn

supports_vision.title: Supports Vision
supports_vision.description: Whether the endpoint accepts image input

extraction_strategy.title: Extraction Strategy
extraction_strategy.description: How to recover the translation (auto, xml_tag, raw, cp)

deployment_backend.title: Deployment Backend
deployment_backend.description: Self-hosted stack serving this model (ollama, vllm, …)

ProviderEditRequest.title: ProviderEditRequest
ProviderEditRequest.description:
One provider block edit from the console.

``extra="forbid"`` so a client that sends a credential gets a 422 naming the
field instead of a silently ignored key. Every field is optional: an edit
submits only what changed, and an omitted field is left untouched in the file.

QESettingsRequest.title: QESettingsRequest
QESettingsRequest.description:
One edit of the ``[defaults]`` QE keys.

``extra="forbid"`` so a client sending ``qe_judge_api_key`` gets a 422 naming
the field rather than a silently ignored key: a judge credential belongs in
the provider block that owns it, not in this form. Every field is optional; an
omitted field is left untouched, and an explicit ``null`` removes it.

QESettingsResponse.title: QESettingsResponse
QESettingsResponse.description:
The quality-estimation gate as the engine will run it.

``engine`` and ``judge_enabled`` are reported separately on purpose: the
pipeline selects the LLM judge on ``judge_enabled`` alone and only warns when
``engine`` says ``tiered`` without it, so the two can legitimately disagree in
a hand-edited file. ``measurable`` is the derived fact the console renders —
without a judge model, no block is scored and the average-QE fields stay at
their ``0.0`` sentinel.

declared_capability.description: Capability flags the provider block states outright. Every other flag is the conservative default, not a measurement of the endpoint.

extraction_strategy.description: How the translation is recovered from the completion

RuntimeActiveModel.title: RuntimeActiveModel
RuntimeActiveModel.description: The provider and models the engine will actually call, right now.

provider_config_source.title: Provider Config Source
provider_config_source.description: Where provider settings live (ubt.toml or the UBT_* environment)

credential_source.title: Credential Source
credential_source.description: Where the credential comes from when the console may not write it

can_write_credential.title: Can Write Credential
can_write_credential.description: True on a loopback, non-strict deployment. False means the console must not offer a credential field at all, and says why

frozen_fields_changed.title: Frozen Fields Changed
frozen_fields_changed.description: Deployment-bound fields edited in the file that need a restart. They are decided once at boot, so reporting them is the difference between a control that works and one that silently does nothing

RuntimeConfigResponse.title: RuntimeConfigResponse
RuntimeConfigResponse.description:
Read-only model/provider configuration actually in force.

Credentials are never included: provider blocks are filtered through an
allow-list before they reach this model.

active.title: Active
active.description: True for the provider currently selected

is_default.title: Is Default
is_default.description: True when [defaults] provider names this block. Distinct from ``active``: UBT_PROVIDER / --provider outrank the file, so the panel must be able to show what the file says separately from what runs

available.title: Available
available.description: False when the block could not be loaded

declared.title: Declared
declared.description: True when the operator declared it in [providers.*]

is_alias.title: Is Alias
is_alias.description: True for a bare protocol alias (chat, claude, responses)

alias_of.title: Alias Of
alias_of.description: The canonical wire protocol an alias stands for (``claude`` -> ``anthropic-messages``), or null for a protocol or a declared block

is_protocol.title: Is Protocol
is_protocol.description: True for the four canonical wire protocols (openai-chat, …). They are the names a [providers.*] block should carry; an alias is a shortcut to one of them

credential_issue.title: Credential Issue
credential_issue.description: Why this provider cannot authenticate, as a stable code ('unresolved_variable' or 'missing'), or null when it can. The variable name is not included: it belongs on the single-provider endpoint the operator opens to fix it

RuntimeProvider.title: RuntimeProvider
RuntimeProvider.description: One declared provider, with credentials deliberately omitted.

SegmentEditRequest.title: SegmentEditRequest
SegmentEditRequest.description: A human post-edit of one block's target text (L3 workbench).

SegmentItem.title: SegmentItem
SegmentItem.description:
One finalized block as the workbench grid shows it.

Mirrors :func:`ubt.api.review.serialize_segment`; that function is the
runtime owner, this is the published shape.

SegmentListResponse.title: SegmentListResponse
SegmentListResponse.description: A page of segments plus the filtered total.

is_loopback.title: Is Loopback
is_loopback.description: True when the request arrived on a loopback host

auth_enabled.title: Auth Enabled
auth_enabled.description: True when an API key gate is configured

allowed_bases.title: Allowed Bases
allowed_bases.description: Filesystem roots the server will read/write

disk_free_gb.title: Disk Free Gb
disk_free_gb.description: Free disk space in GB on the db_dir volume

SystemInfoResponse.title: SystemInfoResponse
SystemInfoResponse.description:
The console's security-boundary panel: where this server is reachable and
what it is allowed to touch.

TMBulkEvictRequest.title: TMBulkEvictRequest
TMBulkEvictRequest.description: Delete the exact filtered scope shown in the confirmation dialog.

TMEntryItem.title: TMEntryItem
TMEntryItem.description: One translation-memory row as the console lists it.

content.title: Content
content.description: Raw TMX XML or JSON text

src_lang.title: Src Lang
src_lang.description: Fallback source language for rows without one

tgt_lang.title: Tgt Lang
tgt_lang.description: Fallback target language for rows without one

provenance.title: Provenance
provenance.description: machine = unverified import (cannot downgrade existing human rows)

TMImportRequest.title: TMImportRequest
TMImportRequest.description: Import translation-memory pairs from a TMX or JSON payload (L4 assets).

TMListResponse.title: TMListResponse
TMListResponse.description: A page of the shared translation memory.

TMevictRequest.title: TMevictRequest
TMevictRequest.description: Translation-memory rows to evict, by id.

block_id.title: Block Id
block_id.description: Block the action was invoked from

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: block = only this block, subsequent = this and later blocks, all = whole book

TermPropagationRequest.title: TermPropagationRequest
TermPropagationRequest.description: Replace one offending term surface with its canonical rendering (L3).
